summary.headline: Cohance FY26 revenue fell about 13% to INR22.68 billion; management guides Q1 FY27 as the low point, with growth returning in H2 FY27.
summary.overview: FY26 revenue declined about 13% YoY to INR22.68 billion, with adjusted EBITDA of INR4.77 billion (21% margin) and gross margin of 70.8%. Pharma CDMO was hit by destocking in two large commercial small-molecule products (about INR260 crore impact), API+ fell 8% to INR10.88 billion on shipment delays and the Nacharam formulation disruption (about INR610 million), and Specialty Chemicals fell 2.1% to INR2.913 billion. Management said Q1 FY27 will be weak on revenue and EBITDA, Q2 stable, and growth returning from H2 FY27, with the Middle East-driven freight and input inflation adding 100-150 bps to gross margin pressure in Q1. This was the first call for new Executive Chairman and Group CEO Umang Vohra, who did not give FY27 numeric guidance.

segments.name: Pharma CDMO
segments.commentary: Revenue INR8.89 billion in FY26; commercial products over 70% of standalone revenue; 140+ active projects; Phase 3 pipeline up to 10 programs. Reload conversion above 90%.

segments.name: API+
segments.commentary: Revenue INR10.88 billion, down 8% YoY; top 15 products about half of API revenue; formulation hit by about INR610 million from Nacharam disruption. Two launches slipped into next quarter; H2 performance improved sequentially.

segments.name: Specialty Chemicals
segments.commentary: Revenue INR2.913 billion, down 2.1% YoY on customer program phasing, regulatory timing and generic pressure. FY27 described as a qualification and readiness year, with growth returning in FY28.

guidance_outlook: Q1 FY27 expected to be the low point for both revenue and EBITDA, driven by H2-skewed revenue schedules, Middle East logistics and input cost inflation, and higher operating costs.
Q2 FY27 expected to be stable; growth to return from H2 FY27 on a YoY basis across all three segments, with API+ and CDMO recovering faster than Spec Chem in H1 ordering.
Q1 FY27 gross margin to take a hit of roughly 100-150 bps on FY26 levels, mainly API+; management is negotiating with some customers to pass on part of the cost inflation.
FY27 capex expected at nearly INR3 billion.

Two destocked large commercial molecules expected to return in FY27, amount not quantified. Two new commercial products: four key starting-material orders for one, with revenue mainly in Q2 and Q3 FY27.
No formal FY27 numeric guidance; management said it would come back with guidance later. NJ Bio return to historical margin levels could take more than two years.
capex_capacity: NJ Bio US facility expansion of about $10 million underway to support scale-up, Phase 2 needs and validation readiness; first bioconjugation campaign completed under cGMP in Q4 FY26.
Sapala cGMP oligonucleotide building block facility under validation; follow-on purchase order received.
Capex of INR2.15 billion in FY26 focused on ADC, oligonucleotides, manufacturing infrastructure and quality systems; about INR3 billion planned for FY27.
Nacharam formulation site: production and US supplies have resumed; utilization still normalizing, with alternate-site strategies in use.
demand_pricing: Small molecule CDMO affected by customer inventory adjustments, order phasing and slower reloads; engagement on the two destocked products described as steady.
ADC: three payload DMFs filed in FY26; more payload-linker filings underway; traction in newer payloads including exatecan-linked opportunities.

API+: demand stable across therapies, growth mainly volume-led; some mature molecules saw pricing pressure, largely offset by volume, efficiency and cost actions. About two-thirds of API+ revenue from innovators or large generic/regional leaders.
Oligonucleotides: more than 20 customer audits and visits in recent months; higher-complexity RFPs progressing.
Specialty Chemicals: agrochemical qualification and registration-sample work progressing; OLED in a product-cycle transition; early engagement in electronic materials and semiconductor chemistries.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the INR260 crore destocking impact on two large molecules returns in FY27, and what are the two new commercial products' contributions?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects both destocked molecules to return in FY27 but declined to quantify, citing customer discussions not yet converted to orders. The first new product has four commercial orders for key starting materials, with revenue mostly in Q2 and Q3 FY27; timing for the second is still under discussion.

qa_highlights.question: What were the one-time expenses (about INR109 crore over two years) and what is the ADC revenue contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 one-offs were a about INR195 million inventory provision and about INR126 million customer adjustments. Niche technology share of revenue was 16.2% for FY26. ADC revenue contribution was not disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: What is the H2 recovery outlook by segment and the Q1/Q2 shape?
qa_highlights.answer: Order of weakness is API+ first, then CDMO, then Spec Chem in Q1. Q2 expected stable, with growth from H2 across all three segments as the order book is skewed to H2.

qa_highlights.question: Will H2 growth be measured YoY or against the FY25 base?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth is measured YoY, but management did not rule out being below FY25 levels given the large commercial molecule lost in FY26; the lag from pipeline to revenue will take time.

qa_highlights.question: What makes up the INR671 crore other expenses line?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR400 crore plus is conversion expenditure; about INR260 crore is marketing and SG&A (brand building after the merger, office, travel).

qa_highlights.question: What is the timeline for consolidated margins to return to about 30%, given the standalone-subsidiary gap?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to a 4-5% gap between standalone and subsidiary margins. Sapala is expected to accelerate on Phase 2/3 reloads. For NJ Bio, the investment takes about one year plus validation, so more than two years to return to prior levels.

risks_watch: Q1 FY27 weakness on revenue and EBITDA, plus Middle East-driven freight and input inflation and the pace of customer cost pass-through.
Concentration in a few small-molecule CDMO products nearing generic erosion; management says concentration is falling but gave no figures.
Return timing and value of the two destocked molecules and the two new commercial launches; two further launches depend on clinical outcomes over 12-18 months.
Nacharam formulation site normalization and US supply recovery.
NJ Bio profitability: more than two years to return to prior margin levels.
Governance and information-flow concerns raised by an investor; new management committed to review governance over the next few months.
Disclosure gaps: no ADC revenue split, no customer concentration figures, no quantified FY27 guidance, and limited detail on other expenses.
summary.management_tone: Cautious on near term, with Q1 FY27 explicitly flagged as the low point and a recovery narrative pinned to H2. Management was evasive on quantification (destocking return values, ADC split, FY27 guidance, customer concentration, Phase 3 volumes), repeatedly deferring to later disclosure. Tone was more confident on pipeline breadth, audits and customer engagement.
key_quotes: We believe the business is moving towards a bottoming out phase, with Q 1 FY27 to be the low point.
The focus for FY27 is execution, order conversion, and delivery visibility.

This concentration is changing positively year-on-year, meaning that there is less concentration in FY26 than there was in FY25 and there will be less concentration in FY27 versus FY26 as we continue to develop our customer project pipeline.

growth.why: No numeric FY27 guidance; management guides Q1 FY27 as the low point on revenue and EBITDA, Q2 stable, and YoY growth returning from H2 FY27, backed by Sapala and NJ Bio capacity, two new product starting-material orders, and FY27 capex of nearly INR 3 billion.
